Subject: Access controls & support access — post-call recap

Hi Sarah — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we all have the same next steps: 

Summary of your requirements (call notes):
- PII scope: customer names, emails, transaction IDs, and limited KYC attributes.
- Data residency: primary requirement is US-only (us-east-1) for the initial deployment; potential EU region later.
- Retention: ability to configure retention windows per dataset, and a hard-delete option.
- Logging/audit: comprehensive audit trails for all support and admin actions; 12+ months retention and exportability.
- Access controls: strict RBAC with least-privilege defaults; SSO/SAML + SCIM for provisioning; support access must be ephemeral and auditable; break-glass path with approval and full logging.

Immediate next steps we agreed:
1) I'll send our access-controls summary + support-access guide (attached).
2) Rishi will follow up on commercial/MAF and deliver a draft Mutual Action Plan.
3) Dev and I can schedule a technical deep-dive to walk through break-glass and audit logs (30–45m).
4) You'll share any compliance questionnaire items that require artifacts (SOC2, encryption details).

Attachments: Redwood-Access-Control-Overview.pdf (summary), Redwood-Support-Access-Guide.pdf (support flow)

If anything above is off, please flag. Otherwise, are you available for a technical deep-dive next week (Tue/Wed preferred)?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Access controls & support access — post-call recap

Thanks Marissa — quick clarifications from our InfoSec side: 

1) PII handling: we need explicit confirmation that Redwood supports field-level redaction and the ability to run scheduled deletions (e.g., 30/90/365 day windows) that are irreversible.
2) Support access: we'd prefer a model where support can only request "support-only" sessions that do not expose raw PII unless break-glass is invoked. Can the break-glass flow require 2 approvals (requestor + manager)?
3) Audit logs: must be tamper-evident and exportable to our SIEM (we use Splunk). How are logs signed/stored?
4) Data residency: confirm there's no cross-region replication outside us-east-1 unless explicitly enabled.

We'll also attach a short security questionnaire — please point me to the artifacts we can share (redacted SOC2, encryption-at-rest and in-transit details, KMS info).

Regards,
Sarah Lee
Security Lead, FinTrust
sarah.lee@fintrust.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Hi Sarah — thanks for the follow-ups. Short answers up front, full details below and attached artifacts. Attaching: FT-SupportAccess-MAAP.xlsx, SOC2-sample-report-redacted.pdf

- Field-level redaction & deletes: Supported. We offer field-level masking in transit and the ability to schedule irreversible deletions at configured intervals; permanent deletes can be triggered via console or API and we provide delete receipts.
- Support-only sessions: Yes — by default support sessions are "support_agent" role which hides sensitive fields; full data exposure requires break-glass.
- Break-glass approvals: Configurable. We support 1- or 2-step approvals; for 2-step we can require a manager approval via the console or an external Jira/Okta approval webhook.
- Audit logs & SIEM: Logs are exported in JSON and can stream to Splunk/Datadog via our logging connector. Logs are stored in an append-only, signed format and encrypted at rest with customer/KMS-managed keys. Retention is configurable; default export retention is 365 days.
- Data residency: You can pin resources to us-east-1. No cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled in org settings.

Next steps we propose:
1) Marissa to share the Mutual Action Plan (MAF) draft. (Attached workbook with timelines)
2) We'll provide the redacted SOC2 and the support-access guide (attached).
3) Schedule a 45m technical deep-dive with Dev to walk the break-glass flow and SIEM export.

Are you available Thurs Feb 18 or Tue Feb 23 for the deep-dive?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Re: Access controls & support access — technical details on RBAC & break-glass

Sarah — following up with the technical specifics so your engineers and infosec have something concrete to review.

Quoted for context:
> On Tue, Feb 16, 2027 at 9:04 AM Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@fintrust.com> wrote:
> > Can the break-glass flow require 2 approvals (requestor + manager)?

RBAC model (out-of-the-box roles):
- owner: full control over org, billing, region pinning.
- admin: manages configs, users, role assignments.
- viewer: read-only; cannot see masked PII fields.
- support_agent: limited support-only role — by default this role receives masked responses and has no access to raw PII.

Support access flow (ephemeral):
1) Support agent initiates a session request in the console or via API.
2) If session requests default to masked view, they receive masked fields.
3) To escalate to full data view (break-glass): request flows to configured approvers. We support 1- or 2-step approval.
4) Once approved, the system issues a time-limited token (default TTL 1 hour, configurable) tied to the approver and requestor identity.
5) All actions during the session are logged with full request/response and KV cache access.

Audit/logging specifics:
- Logs are written to an append-only store and signed using your org KMS key if you supply one; otherwise Redwood KMS is used.
- Logs are exported as compressed newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) to your S3 bucket or streamed to Splunk via our connector.
- Tamper-evidence: log blocks are chained and signatures available for verification.
- Retention: configurable per-project; we can provision a default of 365 days and offer archival for 7 years if needed.

Data residency & replication:
- Resources (models, KV caches, logs) are pinned to a region (e.g., us-east-1). No cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled.

Break-glass operational controls (examples):
- Break-glass requires an approval ticket (console approval or external webhook).
- Automated notifications to security mailing list and Slack channel when break-glass occurs.
- Post-incident review package: we can generate a zip with session transcript, approver IDs, and all related logs for audit.

If helpful, I can send a short runbook and a demo recording of the break-glass flow. We can also run the deep-dive as a screenshare and demo a live request.

— Dev Patel
